news.Title: IonQ vs. Alphabet: Which is the Better Quantum Computing Stock to Own for Next 5 Years?
news.Content:
While AI gets all the headlines, quantum computing is starting to become a technology that's becoming more and more interesting. Several companies are making strides in quantum computing endeavors, and the technology is only years away from being commercially viable.

The big question investors must answer in this space is whether it's best to go with a massive company that has huge resources that can make a successful quantum computer, or if it's better to back a pure-play company that is much smaller.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Two of the most popular options in this segment are Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and IonQ (NYSE:IONQ), with Alphabet being the giant and IonQ the smaller player. It's the classic David versus Goliath matchup, but which one makes the most sense? It all depends on your risk tolerance.

Image source: Getty Images.

IonQ is making huge strides

When comparing Alphabet's and IonQ's quantum computing technologies, it is a bit difficult to draw direct comparisons. IonQ releases information about every breakthrough it makes and keeps the investing public well informed of its progress. Alphabet is more silent, although it does release updates about its quantum successes from time to time.

At the surface level, some may think that Alphabet is being silent because it's behind and doesn't want to publicly display that information, but I don't think that's what's going on.

IonQ doesn't have a business to fund its operations. It must find partners and raise capital to continue its operations. Unless IonQ can show these entities that it's making progress and that its technology is coming along nicely, it won't be able to drum up enough interest to keep its company going.

On the flip side, Alphabet is self-funding its quantum research. It only has to keep internal leaders happy with progress, and staying under the radar is a smart idea on their part. So, it's natural that Alphabet doesn't release as many updates as IonQ.

But that doesn't mean IonQ is behind by any means.

Next year, it's releasing its Superion 256-qubit quantum computer. With IonQ's backlog rising to $1.2 billion, it has generated a lot of interest. While this machine isn't quite ready for commercial-level workloads, it's a step in the right direction, and several clients are ordering the machine so they can start to develop quantum computing programs for future implementation. Depending on how this launch goes, it could vault IonQ into a leadership position. It also has plans to build a 10,000-qubit computer, which would be the first commercial-level computer ready for purchase. That's still a few years out, but with quantum technology progressing rapidly, it will be here before investors know it.

Story Continues

But does that make it a better buy than Alphabet for a quantum-focused investment?

IonQ isn't for everyone

IonQ isn't a stock that everyone should own. In fact, I would argue that most shouldn't. Why? Its chance of success is low. While Alphabet hasn't been public with its quantum computing products, the reality is that its products are competitive with IonQ and boast similar fidelity. Alphabet isn't the only big tech company , either. Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) and IBM (NYSE:IBM) are also heavily investing and represent well-funded competition to IonQ.

If IonQ works out, it will be a huge winner. But there's high risk involved because if it loses to any of its peers or the big tech companies, the stock could plummet to $0. IonQ is a high-risk, high-reward investment. If investors want exposure to quantum computing without the risk of extreme failure, then Alphabet makes for a great stock pick . If you're OK with more risk in exchange for upside, then IonQ is a smart option. Just be sure to size the position appropriately to account for the risk.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again

In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. If you'd invested $5,000 then, you'd be sitting on $1,897,590 today.*

Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. It's a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast.

Continue »

news.Title: Prediction: Here’s Where Alphabet Stock Will Be in 5 Years
news.Content:
There's a lot of concern over what the future holds for Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL). The internet company has transformed from an asset-light business into an extremely asset-heavy business, as it and its hyperscaler peers are set to spend trillions of dollars building new data centers for artificial intelligence over the next few years.

That shift has led to a significant sell-off in the stock. Shares are down 30% from their peak in late spring. The biggest culprit is Alphabet's negative free cash flow in each of the last two quarters, as well as management's commentary suggesting cash burn could push even deeper into the red next year.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

With the stock trading at just 21 times forward earnings, the market isn't expressing much faith that the business will produce meaningful returns on its invested capital. That's despite financial results and management commentary suggesting it could quickly see a cash-flow turnaround and head much higher. Here's my prediction for where Alphabet stock trades in five years.

Image source: Getty Images.

A huge investment cycle could pay off massively

Alphabet plans to spend between $195 billion and $205 billion on capital expenditures this year. CFO Anat Ashkenazi also said she expects capex "to increase significantly in 2027."

Analysts expect Alphabet's cash burn to peak in 2027. For the full year, Alphabet could spend $80 billion more in cash than it brings in. 2028 could see it burn through another $50 billion. But free cash flow could turn positive again in 2029.

Importantly, Alphabet ended the third quarter with $56 billion in cash and about $209 billion in marketable equities. That puts it on strong financial footing and gives it multiple ways to fund the continued build-out of its AI data centers: It can use its cash, sell its marketable equities (once lock-ups expire), sell more debt, or raise cash via its own equity.

All that cash is going toward building new data centers (which have a useful life of 40 years) and outfitting them with servers and networking equipment (which have a useful life of six years). About 65% of spending is currently going toward the latter this year.

Over time, however, a much higher percentage should go toward revenue-generating servers, reducing the business's capital intensity and enabling it to generate strong free cash flow .

Story Continues

The results are already showing up in Alphabet's cloud computing segment. The steep ramp-up in spending that started in 2023 has led to accelerating Google Cloud revenue growth. That includes revenue growth exceeding 100% in the most recent quarter, indicating the delay between spending and revenue generation. But the payback period on Alphabet's spending is getting shorter.

Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian says its payback period for the average server on Google Cloud Platform is about two years. But the payback period for its own Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) systems is less than half of that. With a useful life of six years and the amount Alphabet is spending on servers, the cash-generating ability of these investments over the useful life is absolutely massive.

Alphabet's Cash flow is set to explode by the end of the decade

With a further step-up in spending in 2026 and 2027, investors should expect continued growth in Google Cloud revenue in 2028 and 2029. Beyond those years, more stable spending should result in significant cash generation. In fact, analysts currently expect Alphabet's free cash flow, excluding stock-based compensation, to reach $305 billion by 2031.

With that level of free cash flow generation, Alphabet stock should be worth significantly more than it is today. Prior to the start of the investment cycle in 2023, Alphabet shares traded around 30 times free cash flow. If it can recover that multiple in 2031 while generating $300 billion in free cash flow (less than analysts currently expect), it'll be worth $9 trillion total.

Considering the stock currently sports a market cap of less than $3.5 trillion, that could be a fantastic return for shareholders over the next five years. It's even a safe bet if you expect management to dilute shareholders by issuing more equity to raise capital over the next few years. But more than likely, it'll offset that dilution with massive buybacks in the outer years once it starts printing hundreds of billions of cash.

news.Title: Follow the Smart Money: 4 AI Stocks Billionaire Dan Loeb Just Bought
news.Content:
Dan Loeb is widely considered one of the world's top investors, starting his Third Point hedge fund with a few million dollars in 1995 and turning it into an over-$28 billion behemoth. In Q3 2026, he was busy scooping up several artificial intelligence (AI) stocks , including Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), and Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META).

Let's look at what may have attracted Loeb to these names.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

1. Nvidia

Loeb's buy of Nvidia shares came before CEO Jensen Huang stepped down, but the company remains in the pole position in the AI infrastructure build-out. Nvidia today is more than just a graphics processing unit (GPU) provider, offering a complete AI factory solution that includes networking, central processing units (CPUs), language processing units (LPUs) for the decode phase of inference , its Nemotron open-weight models, and an expanding software layer.

That package has helped Nvidia increase its revenue per gigawatt from around $18 billion when it introduced its Hopper architecture a few years ago to around $40 billion today with Vera Rubin.

With future memory and manufacturing capacity locked in, along with its strong ecosystem, expect Nvidia to remain the AI infrastructure leader over the coming years.

2. SpaceX

SpaceX is one of the most exciting companies on the planet as it looks to disrupt industries and conquer space. The company recently achieved a major milestone by catching the upper stage of its Starship rocket, setting it up to fundamentally change the economics of space launches as it moves toward rapid reuse. This is also a stepping stone for SpaceX to hit some of its loftier goals, such as orbital data centers, Earth-to-Earth transport, and asteroid mining.

Back on Earth, SpaceX has become one of the world's largest neocloud companies and plans to rapidly grow its AI infrastructure-as-a-service business. Right now, it is getting great rates on its AI infrastructure through short-term rentals, allowing it to see a payback on its investments within a year. The company also plans to disrupt the U.S. mobile market, and its Cursor AI coding platform is growing quickly.

Image source: Getty Images.

3. Microsoft

Microsoft continues to see strong growth in both its Azure cloud computing unit and its enterprise software business. Azure has been a persistent 30%-plus revenue grower, with its revenue growth hitting 48% last quarter. With significant commitments from OpenAI and an overall $677 billion backlog, Azure should remain a strong growth driver in the years ahead.

Story Continues

At the same time, the company has been gaining significant traction with its AI Copilot assistants across Microsoft 365 and its GitHub code repository. The shift to a seat-plus-consumption model has been paying off, and Copilot usage has been surging, with it seeing an eightfold year-over-year increase in seats last quarter. Given how embedded the company's software and governance tools are in the enterprise space, it looks well positioned to emerge as an AI software-as-a-service (SaaS) winner.

4. Meta Platforms

Meta Platforms has been one of the best companies at using AI to drive growth in an already established, strong business. It's employing AI to both keep users on its apps longer by displaying more content they are interested in and to feed them more relevant ads. This is leading to higher ad loads, stronger conversions, and better ad pricing.

Last quarter, its revenue surged 26%, with a 14% increase in average price per ad and a 10% jump in ad impressions.

Perhaps more exciting, though, is that Meta is jumping headfirst into consumer AI agents. These agents can help users with a multitude of tasks, but Meta will benefit most when they make purchases on a user's behalf. Here, Meta will get a cut of the transaction fee, giving it another potential new large revenue stream and putting it at the forefront of agentic commerce.

news.Title: Amazon's re:Invent Conference Starts Nov. 30. Here's What the Stock Did in the Month After the Last 10.
news.Content:
Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) has a big week ahead. Its cloud computing arm, Amazon Web Services (AWS), hosts its yearly re:Invent conference in Las Vegas from Monday, Nov. 30, to Friday, Dec. 4. AWS calls re:Invent its flagship annual conference, and it's where the unit launches many new products every year.

It's tempting to think the stock might get a boost when AWS shows off what it's built. To find out, I checked how Amazon shares did in the month after each of the past 10 conferences, from 2016 through 2025, and compared that with the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Shares trade near $257 as I write, up about 12% this year and well ahead of the S&P 500 's rise of about 5%. Amazon now stands about 9% below its Aug. 3 record close of $284.02.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Has the stock usually risen after re:Invent?

Not really. For every year, I measured from the close on the trading day before the conference started to the close a month after opening day, using the same window for the S&P 500.

Amazon stock rose in just four of the 10 windows. It beat the index in four of them, too. And its median return was a drop of around 0.7%, but the S&P 500's median was a gain of about 2.1%.

The best year was 2024, when Amazon climbed around 6% in the month after the conference while the index dropped about 3%.

The worst was 2022. Other factors can easily outweigh a week of product news, and that year the stock had already lost about 44% before the conference began. It slid another 12% in the month that followed, compared with a 6% decline in the S&P 500.

Last year was closer to a wash. After the event ran from Dec. 1 to Dec. 5, 2025, Amazon stock slipped about 1% for the month, while the index was about flat.

In short, there's no consistent post-conference rally in the record. Amazon has lagged the S&P 500 more often than not after re:Invent -- in six of those 10 windows.

The product launches: a mixed record

The week of the conference hasn't been much better. Measured from the previous close to that Friday's close, Amazon stock fell during six of those 10 conference weeks.

The 2024 event makes the strongest case that AWS's news can matter. That year, AWS rolled out its Nova family of artificial intelligence (AI) models and made servers built with its Trainium2 AI chips available to customers. Amazon shares climbed every trading day that week and gained around 9%, while the S&P 500 added about 1%.

Story Continues

But last year's lineup was arguably just as big. AWS made servers built with its next-generation Trainium3 chips available and unveiled its Nova 2 models, and the stock dipped about 2% in the conference week.

What does seem to move Amazon stock is its quarterly reports. Shares surged around 15% on July 31, the day after Amazon released its second-quarter results. In one day, the stock moved more than it did in any of those 10 post-conference months.

AWS is growing faster

That makes sense, because AWS is where most of Amazon's profit comes from.

In the third quarter of 2026, AWS posted $17.8 billion in operating income, up 55% year over year. This was around 63% of Amazon's $28.1 billion in total operating income for the period.

Plus AWS's sales growth keeps accelerating. Its revenue rose 39% in the third quarter, faster than the second quarter's 37% and almost twice the 20% growth AWS had a year earlier.

Of course, all this takes heavy spending. Amazon still expects around $220 billion in cash capital expenditures in 2026, and that could weigh on its free cash flow for a while. And the stock isn't cheap, at about 25 times earnings based on what analysts expect for 2027. But with AWS growing almost twice as fast as it was a year ago, I think the price is fair.

So, is the month after re:Invent a good time to own Amazon stock? Going by the last 10 years, not especially. After all, four weeks is a short window, and I wouldn't use the record as a reason to rush in before the conference or to wait till after it.

I'd consider buying Amazon shares for the growth AWS keeps posting every quarter. I just wouldn't time my purchase around Nov. 30.

news.Title: Billionaire Bill Ackman’s Top 5 Stocks After Selling Stakes to Open a Brand-New Position
news.Content:
Bill Ackman doesn't own many stocks, so every change in his portfolio is a statement. His latest 13F, filed November 16 for the quarter ended September 30, shows the billionaire trimming several of his biggest bets and putting the money into two new names.

Ackman founded Pershing Square in 2004 with about $54 million and turned it into one of the most closely watched concentrated portfolios on Wall Street. This quarter, the firm reported about $30.8 billion in holdings, including a $10.3 billion position in Pershing Square Inc. itself.

The selling was broad. Ackman cut his stake in a software giant by about 35%, just months after first buying it on what he called a compelling valuation. He also trimmed the Facebook parent by 11%, two leaders in card networks by 11% to 12%, the alternative asset manager by about 11%, and the Burger King parent by 15%. Also, Pershing completely exited its position in a global car rental giant. Even after the trims, the 10 stocks on our list account for about 56% of the reported portfolio.

The proceeds mostly went into two first-time positions. Pershing bought about 6.6 million shares of Intercontinental Exchange, worth roughly $1 billion. The firm sees the exchange operator as a simple, predictable cash generator whose shares had fallen on worries considered unwarranted. Pershing also built a $954 million stake in eye-care company Alcon. Among the existing holdings, Ackman has only added to the streaming leader by about 18%.

The pattern is classic Ackman: sell what has worked or grown too large, and buy durable, cash-generating franchises when the market sours on them. For a closer look at the new exchange bet, see how Intercontinental Exchange stacks up against its biggest rival , and for another billionaire's favorites, see the top stocks in Mario Gabelli's fund .

We covered Billionaire Bill Ackman's top 5 stocks below. You can click to see our expanded list of Bill Ackman's Top 10 Stocks .

Our Methodology

For this list, we scanned Pershing Square Capital Management's 13F portfolio for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, filed on November 16 through Pershing Square Inc., and picked the stocks with the largest percentage of the portfolio. We excluded call and put options, as well as Pershing's $10.3 billion stake in Pershing Square Inc. itself. The stocks are ranked by the value of the fund's stake, and percentages are based on the filing's total reported value of about $30.8 billion.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

Story Continues

You can see the 4 stocks that Bill Ackman and Jim Cramer both agree on in our video by clicking the image below:

5. Howard Hughes Holdings Inc. (NYSE: HHH )

% of Portfolio: 6.66%

Fund's Stake Value: $2.05 billion

Howard Hughes is the most personal bet on this list. Ackman serves as its executive chairman and wants to turn the real estate developer into a diversified holding company, a strategy many compare with Berkshire Hathaway's. Pershing kept its 27.9 million shares unchanged in the quarter.

That transformation is now underway. Third-quarter revenue, reported November 5, jumped 63% to $636.3 million, helped by the first full quarter of Vantage, the insurance and reinsurance group it acquired in June. Same-store operating asset income rose 9%, and management plans to move the real estate business to an asset-light model and redeploy the proceeds into Vantage.

The transition is messy. A $105.4 million loss on the sale of district utility receivables pushed the quarter to a GAAP loss, and Vantage's reported combined ratio was 101.8%, an underwriting loss on paper, though management put the underlying figure at 94.9% excluding purchase-accounting effects.

This is a long-term wager on Ackman's ability to allocate capital. It isn't his only unusual holding, as this stock he shares with two unlikely co-investors shows .

4. Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ: META )

% of Portfolio: 6.67%

Meta is Ackman's bet that the world's biggest social media company can turn AI into better ad targeting and new products. He trimmed the stake by about 11% last quarter, to 2.83 million shares, but a higher share price left the position slightly larger in dollar terms.

The ad business is still accelerating. Third-quarter revenue, reported October 21, rose 26% to $64.6 billion, and CEO Mark Zuckerberg said accounts on its new Muse AI app had topped 10 million. Meta also narrowed its 2026 capital spending range to $135 billion to $145 billion, raising the low end by $5 billion.

The cost of that ambition is showing up in the cash flow. Capital expenditures reached $34.9 billion in the quarter, free cash flow turned negative at about $2.1 billion, and a $9.89 billion litigation charge pulled profit well below expectations.

Ackman's trim reads as risk control on a holding whose spending keeps climbing. Whether Muse can justify that spending is the open question, which we looked at here .

3. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT )

% of Portfolio: 6.77%

Fund's Stake Value: $2.08 billion

Microsoft is the clearest sign that Ackman is willing to change his mind quickly. Pershing first disclosed the stake in May, calling the valuation compelling after a selloff, and added about 10% in the second quarter. In the third quarter, it sold roughly 35% of the position, leaving 4.06 million shares.

The sale doesn't reflect a weaker business. In its fiscal first quarter, reported October 28, Microsoft's revenue of $92.3 billion beat estimates, Azure grew 48%, and commercial remaining performance obligations jumped 73% to $677 billion, a huge backlog of contracted cloud demand.

The tension is spending. Capital expenditures more than doubled to about $39.4 billion in the quarter, and investors are still waiting to see that build-out turn into higher free cash flow. With the shares up roughly 37% between the June and September filings, Ackman may simply have taken profits.

Even after the cut, Microsoft remains his third-largest stock holding. Whether Azure can outgrow its own costs is the debate, which we covered in depth .

2. Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN )

% of Portfolio: 6.88%

Fund's Stake Value: $2.12 billion

Amazon has been a steady core holding for Ackman, even as he managed its size. After cutting the stake by about 26% in the second quarter, he sold less than 1% in the third, keeping 8.51 million shares. Pershing projects Amazon's earnings per share will grow about 24% a year, among the fastest in the portfolio.

The October 29 report supported that view. AWS revenue grew 39% to $46 billion, the unit produced $17.8 billion of operating income, and its backlog reached $578 billion. Revenue commitments for Amazon's in-house Trainium chips rose more than 20x year over year, lowering its dependence on outside chip suppliers.

The catch is the capital bill. Amazon expects about $220 billion of capital spending in 2026, and trailing free cash flow has swung to roughly negative $42 billion. If AI demand cools, that build-out becomes a high fixed cost.

Ackman is betting that today's spending creates tomorrow's earnings power, as it did in Amazon's past. Whether investors are underrating its competitive edge is a fair question, as we explored here .

1. Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: UBER )

% of Portfolio: 7.62%

Fund's Stake Value: $2.35 billion

Uber is Ackman's largest stock holding, and he barely touched it last quarter, keeping about 34.3 million shares. Pershing projects Uber's earnings per share will grow about 25% a year – the fastest among its holdings. The company's latest results confirm it.

Third-quarter gross bookings, reported November 4, rose 20% to $59.8 billion, and trips grew 16% to 4.1 billion. Adjusted EBITDA climbed 31% to $3.0 billion, and non-GAAP EPS rose 35% to $0.88. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi called it the fifth consecutive quarter of 20%+ Gross Bookings growth. Uber guided fourth-quarter bookings to $63.25 billion to $65.25 billion.

The debate is robotaxis. Uber expects about 700 fully driverless vehicles on its platform by the end of 2026 and more than 2,000 in 2027, but self-driving rivals could eventually bypass its network. GAAP profit was also dented by a $476 million loss on revaluing equity investments.

Ackman is betting Uber becomes the platform autonomous fleets need, not their victim. Whether it can keep growing as robotaxis spread is the central question, which we tackled here .

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of UBER as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Apple (AAPL) Grows at 12% and Trades at 37 Times Earnings. Is It Worth It?
news.Content: We just published a list of the Top 10 Stocks to Buy According to Billionaire George Soros , and Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL ) ranked 6th on this list. George Soros made his name betting against currencies and central banks, and that record is still the reference point for macro investing decades later. Born in Budapest in 1930, he built his fortune running the Quantum Fund, and the firm that carries his name has been investing for more than five decades. Soros Fund Management is no longer a hedge fund in the ordinary sense. It returned outside money years ago and now runs as a family office, which means it has no outside investors to report to and can hold a position for as long as it likes. That freedom shows up in the filings. The firm's latest quarterly disclosure, covering the three months to the end of September and filed in the middle of November, lists 263 separate positions worth about $8.51 billion in total. What stands out is the composition rather than the size. Two of the three largest disclosed positions were put options on energy index funds rather than holdings of shares, and a further $1.17 billion sits in convertible notes. Positions in shares account for a little under two-thirds of the total. Concerned about what rising rates do to a portfolio like this? Check out our list of the 10 Best Stocks to Buy for a Rising Interest Rate Environment . Strip out the hedges and the debt, and the common stock that remains falls into two camps that have almost nothing in common. One is artificial intelligence, held through chipmakers and the platforms building data centres. The other is regulated electricity, held through utilities whose earnings are set by state commissions rather than by the market. That pairing is not an accident. The same demand that makes the chips valuable makes the power valuable, and the utilities get paid whether or not any particular model works. Does the AI trade still have room to run? Here are the 10 Undervalued AI Stocks to Buy Now . One caveat matters more than usual this quarter. A quarterly filing is a photograph taken on the last day of September, and the market has moved hard since. The technology names in this portfolio have mostly fallen since that date, one of them by more than half, while the utilities and the non-technology holdings have gained. The figures below are the values recorded on the last day of the quarter rather than the prices available today. ALSO READ: 10 Best Fundamental Stocks to Invest in According to Billionaires Story Continues Apple Inc. was the sixth largest common stock holding in Soros Fund Management's portfolio at the end of September, with a stake worth $131,103,314, or 1.54% of the firm's disclosed holdings. We rank these positions by the value of the stake recorded on the last day of the quarter, and we exclude put and call positions, convertible notes and exchange-traded funds, so that every name is a holding of common stock in an operating company. Beyond Soros Fund Management, Insider Monkey's database shows 165 hedge funds held Apple Inc. at the end of the third quarter of 2026, down from 169 three months earlier. Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. news.Title: Morgan Stanley sends a strong signal to Google stock investors
news.Content:
Google (GOOGL) has a credibility problem with its own investors. The company built the infrastructure that made the current AI boom possible, only to watch competitors define the narrative about where AI is headed next.

Its stock has reflected that frustration, trading near the bottom of a 52-week range even as the company's most significant new product in years rolled out to hundreds of millions of users.

Morgan Stanley equity analyst Brian Nowak is not ignoring the disconnect. In a note shared with TheStreet, he laid out five takeaways from a product launch that most of the market has not yet priced in.

That product is Gemini Tasks. It is Google's consumer AI agent, now free and available to roughly 250 million users in six countries. Nowak rates Alphabet (GOOGL) Overweight with a price target of $375.

What Gemini Tasks puts in front of 250 million users

Users reach Tasks through a toggle inside the existing Gemini interface, with no separate download required. The note shared with TheStreet put Gemini's total monthly active user base at more than 1 billion. That makes the distribution problem most consumer AI apps face at launch irrelevant here. The agent was in front of a global installed base from day one.

Also read: Michael Burry sees a serious problem Wall Street may be overlooking

The initial feature set covers calling, with the agent waiting on hold, and automatically booking appointments. Shopping integrates Google Pay with optional spending caps.

A password manager connection allows the agent to log in to accounts and take actions on the user's behalf. Gmail, Calendar, Google Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Slides are all connected through Tasks. Google Flights, Hotels, YouTube, and YouTube Music round out the first-party integrations.

For Google, agentic connections at launch total more than 60, including Instacart, OpenTable, WhatsApp, Ticketmaster, and Spotify, compared with Meta Muse, which has more than 100 current connections. Morgan Stanley noted in the note that both platforms need to grow those numbers significantly before the agent becomes a default tool for most consumers.

The number Morgan Stanley keeps coming back to

The figure Nowak uses in the note shared with TheStreet is $30 trillion. That is his estimate of consumer spending that agentic AI platforms could eventually handle.

It covers purchases made today through direct search and manual booking flows: e-commerce, travel, restaurant delivery, logistics, and advertising. None of that currently runs through a persistent AI agent.

Story Continues

Morgan Stanley described these offerings as "a market-cap moving opportunity and material source of potential ROIC on GenAI investment." The firm said Google has entered the race in a way that lets it scale faster than a standalone app competitor, since its user base is already in place.

One driver of that case is Gemini 4 Hydrogen's 4X compute efficiency improvement over the Gemini 3.8 Flash model, which shipped in September. Lower compute costs make it economically viable to serve more users at a higher frequency.

Meta has said it is targeting a 10X efficiency gain for Muse in 2027. Morgan Stanley said in the note that efficiency improvements are "critical to lowering cost to serve and delivering ROIC."

Why search cannibalization is the investor question that matters most

Google's search business generates an effective 20% to 40% of transaction value from the commerce it touches, according to the note shared with TheStreet. Consumer AI agents including Meta Muse operate on low single-digit commissions. The differential is potentially five to 10 times.

Gemini Tasks is free and runs inside the same interface users already open for search queries. The investor concern is what happens to search revenue when both products compete for the same transaction.

Someone booking a restaurant through Tasks is not running a Google search for restaurants. That activity generates search ad revenue today. Nowak noted in the note shared with TheStreet that how much of Tasks usage will be incremental versus redirected is not measurable from outside the company.

More Google:

Google's AI chips could change what ChatGPT costs you

Google's next TV gadget may do much more than stream

Apple and Alphabet are sending Wall Street different signals

The note is direct on what this means for valuation. Navigating the transition without cannibalizing search "will be important to the multiple investors are willing to put on GOOGL as it will speak to search growth durability." That framing puts cannibalization at the center of what determines the stock's multiple, not just revenue.

Google's scale against Meta's data advantage

Meta Muse has approximately 12 million monthly active users , according to third-party data cited in the note shared with TheStreet. Gemini is above 1 billion monthly active users.

Muse is a standalone app that users have to find, download, and decide to open. Gemini Tasks is a toggle inside a product most of them already use. That gap in the numbers comes down to the difference in distribution.

Meta's data may still matter over time. Its Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp network provides Muse with a social graph and purchase-intent history that Google's search-based user profiles do not fully capture.

Morgan Stanley said in the note it expects deeper integration of that data into Muse and flagged it as a competitive factor to watch as both platforms develop their recommendation layers.

Morgan Stanley's $375 price target implies roughly 34% upside from Alphabet's Nov. 17 close. The bull case of $450 and bear case of $225 reflect substantially different assumptions about how the cannibalization question is resolved and how quickly the agent scales. At $280.20, the stock sits closer to the midpoint between the bear case and the base case than to the base case itself.

Analyst consensus across Morgan Stanley's coverage shows 88% of analysts rate Alphabet Overweight and 12% rate it Equal-weight, with no Underweight ratings. The share price gap versus that consensus reflects what the market is pricing in as uncertainty around the agentic transition, and how much of the $30 trillion opportunity the company will capture without trading away the search revenue it already has.

news.Title: Cisco vs. HPE: One Has Better Financials, the Other Has 93% Upside. Which Stock Wins?
news.Content:
Did you know some of AI's biggest opportunities may be hiding in plain sight, right behind Big Tech? Even as chipmakers get all the spotlight, AI still relies on networking, servers, and security to keep everything running. These businesses don't always make the biggest headlines, but they're absolutely essential to the AI buildout.

Cisco (CSCO) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) are perfect examples. Both have their respective AI initiatives, and the best part is they pay dividends, too. Let's see where these two companies stand today

More News from Barchart

Disney Just Boosted Its Dividend by 33%. That Gives DIS Stock Investors a Real Reason to Stick Around.

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

Cisco (CSCO): A Leader in AI Networking and Cybersecurity

The aftermath of COVID-19 highlighted the critical role of video meetings, cloud-based software, and online transactions. Behind those is Cisco, one of the crucial companies that keeps those connections running.

Cisco is also adapting to the AI revolution, announcing new capabilities for its AI Defense and IQ platforms, designed to identify gaps in AI systems and threats that could arise across a business network.

Today, the company is worth $383 billion and is the larger of the two.

Hewlett Packard (HPE): Building Its Position in AI Infrastructure

The other company worth highlighting is HP Enterprise (not the laptop and printer brand). This is often confused, as Hewlett Packard Enterprise is different from HP after its split in 2015. HPE makes servers and systems that help companies manage data.

HPE is making a huge leap forward in AI infrastructure with its latest supercomputer, which ranked 14th worldwide in November 2026. Similar to Cisco, this achievement strengthens HPE's position in large-scale AI computing.

Still, HPE is the smaller company, with a market cap of $60 billion.

Different businesses with the same interest in AI. Let's look under the hood to see how their initiatives translate into numbers.

CSCO vs. HPE: What Do the Financials Reveal?

I gathered these data from the Barchart Stock Screening Tool, and here's how they stack up:

Right off the bat, Cisco takes the lead, with annual sales climbing 11.8% year over year to $63.3 billion, while HPE's sales grew 13.8% to $34.3 billion. So HPE is growing a little faster, but Cisco still brings in nearly twice as much revenue.

Story Continues

That gap widens even more when we look at profitability. Cisco's annual net income jumped 30.3% to $13.3 billion, whereas HPE's plunged 97.8% to just $57 million, partly because of $1.6 billion in impairment charges tied to its Hybrid Cloud business.

The same pattern shows up in return on equity, where Cisco comes in at 32.6% compared with HPE's 15.5%. Cisco lands the final blow with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.38, lower than HPE's 0.65, suggesting the company relies less on debt relative to shareholder equity.

So Cisco clearly wins the financial comparison, but there's still one more important metric for income-focused investors to consider, and that's dividends.

Cisco vs. HPE: Which Stock Pays Better Dividends?

Forget the financials for a moment; here's what investors can expect from these two companies.

CSCO pays a forward annual dividend of $1.68, translating to a yield of approximately 1.77%, and its dividend payout ratio is at ~41%. This suggests that the majority of the earnings are reinvested in the business.

Meanwhile, HPE pays $0.57 per share annually, which translates to a yield of about 1.25%. It has a dividend payout ratio of ~19%, which is more conservative than Cisco. But it also means the company has more room to increase dividends in the future.

Cisco vs. HPE: Which Stock Does Wall Street Favor?

Now, how does Wall Street value these companies?

A consensus among 26 analysts rates CSCO stock a "Moderate Buy". It has a 58% upside potential if it reaches its high target prices.

With HPE, it's pretty even, as a consensus among 21 analysts rates HPE stock a "Moderate Buy," too, but with a much higher upside potential of about 93% if it reaches its high target price.

Cisco vs. HPE: Which Stock Is the Better Buy Now?

Both Cisco and HPE are worth watching as they expand their positions in AI infrastructure. However, in this heavyweight-versus-challenger matchup, Goliath wins by a landslide.

Cisco's better financials and payouts today make it the better buy, at least for me. But I wouldn't count HPE out, especially with its growing sales and progress in its AI initiatives. If it regains its footing, there could be significant upside for investors willing to wait.

Cisco takes the crown today, but HPE remains a compelling case worth keeping on the radar.

news.Title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 20: Amazon Shares Slide on AI and Mega-Cap Tech Sell-Off
news.Content:
Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), a global e-commerce, cloud, and digital advertising platform, closed at $246.82, down 4.10%. Shares fell on Friday amid an AI and mega-cap tech sell-off, while investors are watching capital spending, margins, and AWS growth.

Trading volume reached 72.1M shares, coming in about 79% above its three-month average of 40.2M shares. Amazon.com IPO'd in 1997 and has grown 251,971% since going public.

How the markets moved today

S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) closed at 6,910, down 3.7%, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) finished at 22,617, down 5.28%. Among broadline retail and cloud computing peers, Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) closed at $127.95, up 1.52%, while eBay (NASDAQ:EBAY) closed at $115.59, down 1.39%; Walmart's stronger holiday outlook highlighted steadier consumer demand than Amazon.com's pressure points.

What this means for investors

Negative sentiment from both its e-commerce and AWS segments seemed to weigh on Amazon stock today.

Soft consumer spending and an increased need for promotional discounting led it to underperform retail counterparts like Walmart, which, as previously mentioned, rose in today's trading session.

Moreover, capital expenditures (capex) continue to weigh on the stock. The company's plan to spend $220 billion has led to free cash outflows, a concerning sign for a company that generated tens of billions in annual free cash flow until recently. Furthermore, despite a massive amount of liquidity, it has had to turn to the debt markets in a rising-rate environment.

Such concerns were not unique to Amazon, and every stock in the Magnificent Seven , which contend with many of the same challenges, dropped today. Additionally, the Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) IPO has put AI in the spotlight this week. That stock has trended down since opening at $111.50 per share yesterday, likely adding to the negative sentiment surrounding AI.

Admittedly, at a P/E ratio of 20, Amazon stock looks like an increasingly attractive buy, arguably making it the one hyperscaler through 2030 that investors should buy and hold. Nonetheless, with Amazon stock caught in the current downturn, investors should probably move cautiously if they choose to invest.

news.Title: Target Shines, Walmart Merely Fine: Two Retail Giants Split on Q3 Results
news.Content:
Walmart WMT shares were down after Thursday's Q3 results, but they were among the few to be in the green on Friday in a broadly down day for the market. Unlike Target TGT, which had come out with truly impressive results Wednesday morning, Walmart's results were ok; not great, but not bad either.

As we noted about Walmart shares recently, their defensive attributes position them to stand their ground during periods of market turmoil. Market participants are clearly grappling with some weighty questions about the broader AI space, with even the long-awaited Anthropic ANT stock losing ground the day after its successful debut.

Walmart shares' recent struggles notwithstanding, they have outperformed peers like Target TGT and even Amazon AMZN over the last five years, up more than +184.2% vs. +38.5% for Amazon and -19.4% for Target. Walmart's +184.2% gain over the last five years compares to a +69.2% gain for the S&P 500 index.

Unlike this standout performance over the last five years, Walmart shares seem to have lost their mojo this year, even though they appear to be rebounding lately, as the year-to-date performance chart below for Walmart, Target, Amazon, and the S&P 500 index shows.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Walmart shares fell sharply after the last quarterly release on August 20th, reflecting a combination of factors, including a seemingly lower-quality earnings beat (benefiting from tariff refunds), decelerating comp growth, and underwhelming Q3 guidance.

Walmart and other big-box retailers are undoubtedly facing a difficult operating environment, with elevated fuel costs not only adding to consumers' financial burdens but also increasing retailers' expenses. Walmart noted on the Q3 earnings call that elevated diesel and transportation costs have added $2 billion to their cost base this year.

A big worry among Walmart investors is decelerating same-store sales or comp growth, which came in at +2.9% for Q3 vs. +2.6% in Q2 and +4.1% in Q1. Comps were north of +4% in each of the preceding year's quarters.

Target appears to have firmly put its struggles of the last couple of years behind it, with Q3 comps coming in at +5.6% (vs. estimates of +3.07%). This was the third quarter in a row that Target posted better-than-expected comps.

It is important to keep in mind that Walmart shares command a premium valuation, trading at 40X forward 12-month EPS estimates, only modestly below the 10-year high of 45.4X in February 2026. This represents a significant expansion in the valuation premium relative to Target, as the chart below of the two stocks' 10-year valuation history shows

Story Continues

Market participants expect stocks with premium valuation multiples to beat and raise when they report results, which is not what we have been seeing from Walmart lately.

Despite the negative effects of elevated fuel costs on consumer spending and the company's freight costs, Walmart remains better positioned than many others in the space given its value orientation, greater indexing to groceries, and robust digital capabilities. Walmart has consistently gained market share among higher-income households in recent years, which has more than offset affordability-driven softness among lower-income consumers.

With respect to the Retail sector 2026 Q3 earnings season scorecard , we now have results from 24 of the 30 retailers in the S&P 500 index. Regular readers know that Zacks has a dedicated stand-alone economic sector for retail, unlike its placement in the Consumer Staples and Consumer Discretionary sectors in the Standard & Poor's standard industry classification. The Zacks Retail sector includes not only Walmart, Target, and other traditional retailers, but also online vendors like Amazon and restaurant players.

Total Q3 earnings for these 24 retailers that have reported are up +3.5% from the same period last year on +8.4% higher revenues, with 75% beating EPS estimates and 66.7% beating revenue estimates.

Please note that the Zacks Retail sector's Q3 EPS and revenue beats percentages at 75% and 66.7% are meaningfully below the corresponding Q3 EPS and revenue beats percentages for the S&P 500 index as a whole at 82.3% and 75.9%, respectively.

The comparison charts below put the Q3 beats percentages for these retailers in a historical context.

As you can see above, the Retail sector's Q3 revenue beats percentages are tracking below the historical averages for this group of companies, while the sector's Q3 EPS beats are in line with the 20-quarter average.

With respect to earnings and revenue growth rates at this stage, we like to show the group's performance with and without Amazon, whose results are among the 24 companies that have already reported. As we know, Amazon's Q3 earnings were down -2.4% on +12.1% higher revenues, as it missed both EPS and top- line expectations.

The two comparison charts below show the Q3 earnings and revenue growth relative to other recent periods, both with Amazon's results (left side chart) and without Amazon's numbers (right side chart)

As you can see above, earnings for the group outside of Amazon are up +8.2% on a +6.9% top-line gain.

Looking at Q3 for the Zacks Retail sector as a whole, combining the actual results that have come out with estimates for the still-to-come retailers, total earnings for the sector are expected to increase by +3.3% from the same period last year on +8% higher revenues.

For 2026, Zacks Retail sector earnings are expected to increase by +7.6%, with 2027 earnings expected to increase by +21.6%. Excluding Amazon's contribution, earnings growth for the Zacks Retail sector is expected to be +6.9% this year ( vs. +7.6% with Amazon) and +9.7% next year (vs. +21.6% otherwise).

Q3 Earnings Season Scorecard

Through Friday, November 20th, we have seen Q3 results from 468 S&P 500 members, or 93.6% of the index's total membership. Total earnings for these companies are up +28.9% from the same period last year on +14.3% higher revenues, with 82.3% beating EPS estimates and 75.9% beating revenues estimates.

Looking at Q3 as a whole, combining the actual results from the 468 S&P 500 members with estimates for the still-to-come companies, total earnings are on track to increase by +29.8% from the same period last year on +14.9% higher revenues, as the chart below shows.

news.Title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 20: Stocks Plunge as AI Trade Unwinds
news.Content:
Falling 3.70% to 6,910, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) entered a technical correction after a seven-day losing streak, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) dropped 5.28% to 22,618, erasing its annual gains. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) fell 1.93% to 48,147.

Gold prices fell 3.02% to $3,517.24 as of U.S. market close, and the 10-Year Treasury yield slipped 0.10% to 4.91%. Sector-wise, energy and utility stocks gained, while technology and industrials tumbled.

Today's biggest moves

Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) plummeted 14.01% following reports of a potential SEC accounting probe that accelerated a broader unwind of artificial intelligence trades. Broadcom Inc (NASDAQ:AVGO) tumbled 12.26% on unconfirmed reports that Alphabet 's (NASDAQ:GOOG) Google would cut next year's chip shipments. Conversely, UnitedHealth Group Inc (NYSE:UNH)rose after TD Cowen upgraded the stock.

What this means for investors

The sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks accelerated today, as simmering nerves boiled over into widespread loss of confidence. Nvidia's deepening woes only magnified the fallout. The Nasdaq Composite has fallen more than 10% this week, and the S&P 500 officially entered a technical correction after dropping 10% below its record high.

Institutional capital is rotating into defensive sectors, including retail and consumer staples. Walmart Inc (NASDAQ:WMT)gained after raising its full-year forecast in yesterday's earnings. Investors will be watching holiday grocery spending for signs of consumer resilience.

For investors, these dramatic shifts can be scary. It is important to remember that markets have always recovered, even from serious sell-offs, and that in the long term, what matters is staying invested . Holding a diversified portfolio of quality stocks for at least five years is a proven way to build wealth.

news.Title: NiSource: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
news.Content:
On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, NiSource (NYSE:NI) raised its long-term financial guidance while expanding its capital investment commitments. The utility is blending standard regulated energy distribution with power contracts for giant technology facilities.

Three things management said stand out.

1. Data Center Expansion Unlocks $1.75 Billion in Customer Savings

NiSource signed a 20-year agreement with Microsoft, marking its fifth data center power contract across three technology giants. The projects run through Genco, the company's power generation segment, and lower electricity bills for retail customers of NIPSCO, its electric utility subsidiary.

With our recently announced Microsoft agreement, Genco now serves 3 of the largest technology companies in the world, and brings our signed agreements to an expected $1.75 billion in savings to existing NIPSCO electric customers.

-- Lloyd Yates, President and Chief Executive Officer

2. Capital Investment Plan Reaches $40 Billion Through 2033

Executive Vice President Shawn Anderson detailed a new seven-year spending forecast that dedicates $32 billion to core regulated utilities and $8 billion to data center generation. Management expects this capital deployment to support compound annual adjusted earnings per share, or net income divided by outstanding stock, growth of 10% to 11%.

Our new 7-year plan totals $40 billion, including $32 billion of base plan investments and approximately $8 billion of Genco investments, to support data center customers.

-- Shawn Anderson, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer

3. Swift Regulatory Recovery Minimizes Capital Drag

Utilities usually wait years to collect revenues on new construction, creating regulatory lag that drags on cash flows. NiSource uses forward-looking rate structures and tracker mechanisms, which are regulatory processes that let utilities recover specific investment costs quickly, to streamline cash generation.

Our new plan improves our cash efficiency by converting over 90% of our investments into initial recovery within 12 months of investment.

Looking Ahead

Large technology companies are expanding heavily across Northern Indiana, where available land, water access, and fiber networks give NiSource an operational edge over surrounding power grids. Management is watching regulatory approval schedules and construction milestones to ensure projects open on time.

Story Continues

Demand from large load customers remains robust.

-- Michael Luhrs, Executive Vice President, Technology, Customer, and Chief Commercial Officer

The utility couples steady 6% to 8% earnings growth from its base gas and electric utilities with higher-margin growth from data center power contracts. That combination creates two complementary income streams that insulate shareholders from regulatory shifts in any single state.

The complementary nature of these business segments offers a value proposition differentiated in the marketplace today.

news.Title: Marvell Reports Dec. 1. History Says What Its Stock Usually Does Next.
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) will release results for its fiscal third quarter of 2027 (the period ended Oct. 31, 2026) on Tuesday, Dec. 1, with a conference call at 1:30 p.m. Pacific time.

The chipmaker's stock comes into the report at around $138 as I write, off about 56% from its June 4 record close of $316.43. And most of that drop is recent. Marvell shares ended Oct. 28 at around $252, the last trading day before speculation started about a deal for optical parts maker Lumentum Holdings .

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

On Nov. 2, the two companies announced an all-stock deal. After it closes, Marvell's current shareholders will own around two-thirds of the combined company. The growth stock is down about 45% from that Oct. 28 close.

The Dec. 1 report will be Marvell's first full quarterly update since it agreed to buy Lumentum. And if the past three years are any guide, the shares might make a big move the day after.

Matt Murphy. Image source: Getty Images.

The stock has fallen after most recent reports

Marvell reports after the market closes, so the reaction shows up in the next day's trading. Here are its last 12 reports, the stock's close-to-close move the next day, and the revenue growth management guided for the following quarter over the quarter just reported.

Shares dropped the next day seven times and climbed five times.

And the moves were big either way. The average swing was around 12%, and seven of the 12 moves topped 10%.

Why did good quarters so often drive the shares down?

Interestingly, the quarters themselves were almost never to blame. In all 12 reports, Marvell's revenue came in above the midpoint of its guidance.

I think the outlook mattered more. In the six reports in which management guided to next-quarter revenue growth of 6% or lower (with one guide for a decline), the stock fell the next day five times, with an average drop of around 9%.

Story Continues

In the six where it guided for about 8% or more, shares climbed four times, with an average gain of about 6%.

But six reports on either side doesn't prove much, and the pattern has a clear exception. In August 2026, management guided to third-quarter revenue of $3.15 billion, up 15% from the second quarter's $2.74 billion, the second-largest increase in the table. The stock still dropped 10% the next day.

A possible reason is that expectations had risen with the tech company 's share price, which had more than tripled since the March 2026 report.

The fourth-quarter guide is the number to watch

This time, the quarter itself could hold even less surprise than normal. When it announced the Lumentum deal on Nov. 2, Marvell said preliminary third-quarter revenue was in line with its guidance. It kept the $3.15 billion midpoint and tightened the range to plus or minus 2%.

That puts the focus on the fiscal fourth quarter, and the bar is high for a chipmaker helped by demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Marvell's revenue climbed 22% year over year in the final quarter of fiscal 2026. Growth then rose to 28% and 37% in the first two quarters of fiscal 2027. And the $3.15 billion third-quarter midpoint means growth of around 52%, an acceleration for a third straight quarter.

"[W]e expect our revenue growth to accelerate further through the remainder of fiscal 2027," Marvell CEO Matt Murphy said in the company's fiscal second-quarter earnings release.

For growth to keep accelerating in the fiscal fourth quarter, revenue would have to exceed $3.4 billion, or about 7% above the third-quarter midpoint. In other words, a guide that just keeps pace with the third quarter might land right around the line that has split the stock's past reactions.

In the end, I'd expect a big move on Dec. 2 either way, and a down day has been a bit more common than an up day. But I wouldn't read much into one day's move when the Lumentum deal isn't expected to close until the first half of 2028.

Personally, I'd pay more attention to the size of the fourth-quarter guide than to the stock's reaction to it. Shares trade at around 20 times the earnings analysts expect for fiscal 2028, a price that seems reasonable if growth continues to accelerate. And if shares drop again on a guide that still shows accelerating growth, I think the lower price might be worth considering for investors who can ride out more swings like these.

news.Title: Meta's Server Chip Shake-Up Could Hand Nvidia a Win
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

GF Securities says reports of server processor order cuts at Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) and Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ) overstate the weakness in demand. Analyst Jeff Pu's supply chain checks point to a change in which chips Meta plans to buy and a shift in how Microsoft allocates manufacturing capacity.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with META.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The distinction matters for Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) and Advanced Micro Devices ( NASDAQ:AMD ), which are competing for a larger share of data center spending.

Pu said Meta is shifting some orders for x86 processors, mainly Intel's Emerald Rapids chips, toward Nvidia's Grace and Vera CPUs.

He put the shift at more than 500,000 chips and linked it to Meta's rollout of servers for AI agents. Pu said Microsoft's overall order volume was steady, with changes in how capacity was allocated among server manufacturers.

AMD is gaining ground in the x86 market, according to Pu. He pegged its third-quarter share of x86 server CPU shipments at 35.5%, up from 27.8% a year earlier. He forecasts shipments of AMD's next-generation Venice processors will rise to 5.4 million in 2027 from 400,000 in 2026.

Investors Takeaway

AI agents can make repeated model calls, retrieve data and use other software to finish a task. That creates work for general-purpose CPUs alongside the accelerators that run AI models. GF Securities expects total server CPU shipments to rise 29% in 2027, with AI inference driving demand.

The question is whether that demand shows up in customer orders and shipments, and how much Nvidia and AMD capture as buyers rethink which processors they deploy.

news.Title: Anthropic Stocks Jump 17.07% in Record Debut as $26 Billion Chipmaker Placement Lands
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Anthropic ( NASDAQ:ANT ) closed its first trading day at $97.17 at 4:00 p.m. ET on November 19, up 17.07% from its $83 IPO price on Nasdaq. The ride was wild. The first trade crossed at $111.50 at 11:48 a.m. ET, ran to $114.99 a minute later, then sank to $92.72 by 1:18 p.m. as the wider market slid 2%. Roughly 832 million shares changed hands on day one.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Signs with NVDA.

Is ANT fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The deal is the largest on record. Anthropic sold 980 million Class A shares for $81.34 billion in gross proceeds after pricing above its $70 to $78 range. A separate $26 billion non-voting placement at $83 brought in Google and Nvidia at about $10 billion each, AMD at $2.5 billion, Broadcom, Micron and Microsoft at about $1 billion each, and TSMC at $500 million. Amazon holds 14.6% and Google 13.4% after the offering, per the final prospectus. Cloud marketplaces generated about 44% of Anthropic's revenue in the first nine months of 2026, according to Fortune , a reminder of how tightly its sales run through partners that are also rivals.

At the close, GuruFocus puts Anthropic's market value at $1.28 trillion. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of just 10/100, which says the listing has almost no public track record of profitability and only middling balance-sheet strength to grade yet, so the score flags data risk more than business quality. Supply is the next test. Up to 315 million insider shares were eligible to sell from day one, and a further 303 million could unlock on December 15. A record pop does not set a floor, and the first quarterly report will decide whether $1.28 trillion is a starting point or a peak.

news.Title: Broadcom is Overvalued at 17.73X P/E: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Broadcom AVGO shares are overvalued, as suggested by a Value Score of F. In terms of the forward 12-month price/earnings (P/E), AVGO is trading at 17.73X, higher than the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's 16.49X. Broadcom is trading at a higher multiple compared with NVIDIA 's NVDA 10.10X, but at a discount compared with Marvell Technology 's MRVL 20.40X and Advanced Micro Devices ' AMD 30.12X.

AVGO Stock's Valuation

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Is AVGO worth buying at current prices? Let's dig deep to find out.

AVGO's Prospects Suffer From Multiple Challenges

Broadcom shares have underperformed Marvell and AMD year to date (YTD), but outperformed NVIDIA. While AVGO shares have returned 1.9%, Marvell and AMD have appreciated 78.8% and 140.1%, respectively. NVIDIA shares have dropped 18.4% YTD.

AVGO Stock's Price Performance

Broadcom shares have suffered from disappointing near-term guidance and the lack of a meaningful increase to AVGO's longer-term AI outlook. The rising contribution from custom AI accelerators, particularly products incorporating expensive high-bandwidth memory (HBM), is pressuring consolidated gross margins. Broadcom anticipates fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 gross margin of approximately 73%, down from 78% reported in the year-ago quarter.

Broadcom's reliance on six major custom accelerator customers also creates concentration risks. Moreover, shortages of advanced wafers, memory and substrates, alongside delays in data center construction and power availability, could affect the timing of AI infrastructure deployments. Financing arrangements supporting customers such as OpenAI and Anthropic introduce additional contingent liabilities. These concerns, combined with the stock's elevated valuation, warrant a cautious investment stance.

AVGO's Strong AI Growth Boosts Competitive Prowess

Broadcom is benefiting from surging demand for custom AI accelerators and networking solutions as hyperscalers expand their AI infrastructure investments. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, AI semiconductor revenues surged 221% year over year and 54% sequentially to $16.7 billion. The company expects AI semiconductor revenues to reach $21.7 billion in the fourth quarter, representing 236% year-over-year growth. More importantly, Broadcom expects AI semiconductor revenues to reach approximately $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028, supported by accelerating custom accelerator adoption.

Broadcom's relationships with Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta provide substantial visibility into future AI semiconductor demand. The company has strengthened its long-standing partnership with Google through an agreement to develop and supply future generations of Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) and AI networking products. Anthropic is expected to deploy an additional 5 gigawatts of TPU capacity in 2027, followed by an incremental 10 gigawatts in 2028. OpenAI is targeting 1.3 gigawatts of Jalapeno accelerator deployments in 2027 and more than 5 gigawatts in 2028, while Broadcom is also developing multiple generations of Meta's MTIA accelerators.

Broadcom's AI opportunity extends beyond custom accelerators into Ethernet switching, optical interconnects and high-speed connectivity solutions. The company's Tomahawk 6 Ethernet switch offers 100-terabit-per-second capacity, while its next-generation Tomahawk 7 targets 200 terabits per second. Broadcom is also expanding its presence in optical digital signal processors, electro-absorption modulated lasers, vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers and continuous-wave lasers. The company expects AI networking revenues to grow as rapidly as its custom accelerator business over the next few years. This diversified AI portfolio enables Broadcom to benefit from rising networking complexity and bandwidth requirements across AI data centers, supporting its long-term growth outlook.

Story Continues

AVGO's Q4 Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Steady Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $3.82 per share, unchanged over the past 60 days, indicating 96% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Broadcom Inc. Price and Consensus

Broadcom Inc. price-consensus-chart | Broadcom Inc. Quote

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $11.63 per share, down 1.4% over the past 60 days, indicating 70.5% growth from the fiscal 2025 reported figure.

Conclusion

Broadcom's modest 1.9% share price appreciation over the past year and premium valuation may discourage investors seeking immediate upside. Nevertheless, AVGO's rapidly expanding AI semiconductor business, strong hyperscaler relationships, networking leadership and growing software portfolio provide compelling long-term growth opportunities. Robust free cash flow generation and operating leverage further strengthen Broadcom's fundamentals. Although customer concentration, supply constraints and margin pressures remain concerns, Broadcom's ambitious AI revenue outlook supports continued earnings growth. These offsetting factors make holding AVGO shares a prudent strategy for investors seeking long-term exposure to AI infrastructure.

Broadcom currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: European shares post worst week in over a year as AI trade unravels
news.Content:
By Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair and Avinash P

Nov 20 (Reuters) - European shares fell 2% on Friday and marked their steepest weekly decline since late March 2025, as investors unwound AI-linked bets after Anthropic's ‌blockbuster market debut failed to revive confidence in the sector, deepening a selloff that spread beyond ‌technology stocks.

The pan-European STOXX 600 closed down 2% to 625.65 points, logging a weekly loss of more than 5.7%, and registered its fifth ​straight session of declines. The index closed at a six-week low.

Anthropic reached a roughly $2 trillion valuation in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday after a record IPO raise. But the shares dropped on Friday as the high-profile debut did little to ease concerns about the returns on massive AI spending.

Chip-linked stocks such as ASML and STMicroelectronics shed more than 9%, ‌dragging the tech sector down 5.4% in ⁠its steepest one-day fall since October 2025.

The AI trade that has underpinned a global equities rally in recent years came under pressure as investors questioned debt-fuelled spending, while political ⁠uncertainty in the US added to concern over the pace of the sector's expansion.

Investors also worried that a slowdown in AI-related spending could weigh on global economic growth, hurting sectors dependent on economic activity and business investment.

"The amplitude of the ​technology ​selloff is threatening the economic outlook and the latter is ​threatening probably the European cyclical stocks that are ‌not necessarily benefiting from this technology selloff due to this reason, due to the impact that it is going to have on broader economic activity," said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, a senior market analyst at Swissquote Bank.

Cyclical sectors including banks, defense and luxury were among the other major laggards down over 2.5%.

"There's definitely a reassessment of AI and some nervousness around the trade," said Mark Preskett, senior portfolio manager at Morningstar Wealth in London. "Investors are sitting ‌on good profits, so there's clearly some profit-taking. Multiples continue to ​fall for the hyperscalers and especially for semiconductor stocks."

Among other movers, ​Abivax plunged 17.2% after Scorpion Capital disclosed a ​short position in the French biotech firm.

Vallourec tumbled 14.6% after the French steel pipe ‌maker reported a 26% drop in third-quarter core ​profit, citing the impact of ​the Iran conflict and operational disruptions in the US.

Despite this week's losses, the STOXX 600 is up 5.8% year-to-date, outperforming the S&P 500's roughly 3% gain and underscoring the resilience of European equities, which ​recently hit record highs on the ‌back of stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings.

Consumer staples stocks outperformed, with Nestle, Unilever and British American Tobacco up ​more than 1% each as investors sought refuge in defensive sectors.

(Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair and Avinash P ​in Bengaluru; Editing by Janane Venkatraman and Shilpi Majumdar)
